title: Tipper station HMI — WebVisu / VISU (not Aveva)
purpose: Operator-station tipper HMI (CODESYS/WebVisu-style VISU screens at the machine). Primary for tipper faults, alarms, IO diagnostics, manual axis control, and machine-data parameters. Distinct from Aveva building HMI and from Ignition Gateway admin UI — though tipper heartbeats/OPC health are checked via Ignition and may require OptiSweep restart when flatlined.
when_to_use: Tipper alarm / fault at operator station
Need alarm history or IO diagnostics on tipper
Motor replace → VISU_MDS axis parameters / home offsets
After unplanned restart: confirm tipper heartbeats (with Ignition OPC)
not_for: Aveva Overall System / Zone Config / Initialize Tote (use aveva_hmi)
SSMS tipper tables as substitute for reading live VISU alarm text
architecture_notes: Each operator station has two tippers (Day2: 8 stations → 16 tippers).
Ignition OPC reads/writes tipper tags; SorterSweeper tracks tote state at tipper.
WebVisu/VISU is the on-station HMI; Ignition Designer/web view can also read tags.
Heartbeat flatline after Ignition comes up late → restart OptiSweep (OPC path).
Physical tipper actions and LOTO remain operator/customer; FORTNA coaches remotely.

role_paths.operator: Primary user of VISU screens; executes physical tipper/LOTO steps.
role_paths.L1_support: Ask alarm text/color/photo or remote-view VISU if available; do not treat as SSMS how-to.
role_paths.L2_support: Deeper VISU_IO_DIAG / alarm history + SSMS Tipper/Tag/Bits; Ignition OPC + heartbeat.
role_paths.L3_support: Persistent tipper faults, axis/MDS parameter work with OM procedures.

Operator Station Lockout/Tagout Procedure Reference: The documented LOTO steps are: 1) At the operator station HMI, navigate to the 'Visu_Dual_MCP' screen. 2) Press CYCLE STOP. 3) If carriage movement is needed, press JOG, select the corresponding tipper axis, and use the + and – buttons.

Visu_Dual_MCP HMI Screen Reference: This screen is referenced in the lockout/tagout procedure. It contains a CYCLE STOP button and, after pressing JOG, provides axis selection and +/- movement controls for the tipper carriages.

Operator Station Components: The operator station features are identified in Table 3-1 and Figure 3-1. The components are: 1. Tipper, 2. Chute, 3. Stacklight, 4. Plastic curtain, 5. Operator station HMI, 6. Push-buttons, 7. Rotary station.
Operator Station HMI: The operator station includes an HMI screen as one of its components, as listed in Table 3-1 and shown in Figure 3-1.
OptiSweep HMI Interfaces: The three HMI interfaces are: System API, Operator station HMI, and Hospital HMI. The manual details screens associated with each interface in subsequent sections.

OptiSweep HMI Interfaces Overview: The System HMI ties into the existing customer system. The Operator Station HMI and Hospital HMI are separate panels. Each interface has associated screens detailed in the manual.
Operator Station HMI Screen Location: The HMI screen is physically located on the right side of each tipper station. It is used to set parameters and control the tippers.

Operator Station HMI Navigation Methods: Screens can be navigated in three ways: the Next Screen drop-down menu, buttons on the right side of the screen, and buttons on the right side of the physical display. The physical buttons navigate to the same screen as the corresponding on-screen button.

Operator Station Primary Screens: Station operators will only need to use the main control panel screen (F3 button), the data screen (F5 button), and the alarms screen (F6 button). The F3 button navigates to the 'Visu_MCP_Dual' screen, which is the primary screen operators need to use.

Operator Station Function Key Screen Mapping: The function keys map to the following screens: F1 navigates to 'Visu_ManControl', F2 navigates to 'Visu_MDs', F3 navigates to 'Visu_MCP_Dual', F4 navigates to 'Visu_IO_Diag', F5 navigates to 'Visu_Data', and F6 navigates to 'Visu_Alarm'.

Tipper Machine Control Panel (Visu_MCP_Dual) Screen Overview: This screen is identified as the primary screen that station operators will need to use. It includes an informational banner for alarms and messages, navigable via arrows. The screen can be directly selected from a drop-down menu (item 12).
Visu_MCP_Dual AUTO Button: Item 2 in the control panel description. Pressing AUTO is required to restart the system after an E-stop reset.
Visu_MCP_Dual JOG Button: Item 3 in the control panel description. The manual explicitly notes that only maintenance personnel should jog the tipper.
Visu_MCP_Dual Axis Position Indicators (A1, Z1, A2, Z2): Item 10 in the control panel description. An axis being 'out of reference' may cause a tipper fault.
Visu_MCP_Dual Feedrate Override: Item 11 in the control panel description.
Visu_MCP_Dual Fault and E-Stop Reset Sequence: Items 7 and 9 in the control panel description. The AUTO REF button (item 8) is enabled after pressing RESET.

VISU_DATA Screen Overview: The VISU_DATA screen is described in section 4.1.2.2 of the OptiSweep Operation and Maintenance Manual. It is the primary monitoring interface for the operator station, consolidating several key performance indicator (KPI) sections: Tipper Stats, Process Status, RunTime Meters, Operator Stats, and Heartbeat Stats.

VISU_DATA Screen Manual Controls: The screen provides the following manual controls: SEND LEFT TO HOSPITAL button (sends the tote at the left tipper to the hospital), SEND RIGHT TO HOSPITAL button (sends the tote at the right tipper to the hospital), and PAUSE TIPPER button (pauses both tippers).

VISU_MANCONTROL Screen Overview: This screen is part of the Operator Station HMI. It includes an informational banner for alarms/messages, displays the currently logged-in user ID, and provides manual control buttons for system components like tippers and grippers.

VISU_MANCONTROL Informational Banner: This banner is a UI element on the VISU_MANCONTROL screen. It provides a scrolling or navigable list of active alarms and informational messages for the operator or maintenance personnel.

LEFT/RIGHT TIPPER FAULT RESET Button: These are manual control buttons on the Operator Station HMI. They are specific to the left and right tippers and are used to clear a fault condition on the selected tipper.

LEFT/RIGHT TIPPER DISABLE Button: These are manual control buttons on the Operator Station HMI for disabling the left or right tipper. The system provides visual feedback for this state via the stacklight turning solid blue.

VISU_MDS (Machine Data) Screen Overview: The Machine Data screen provides access to axis-specific configuration parameters. A COPY FROM OPPOSITE button is available to copy parameters to the selected axis from the other tipper.

VISU_MDS Axis Parameter Definitions: Key parameters include: MD0 Axis Name, MD1 OT Minus, MD5 Tote Pickup Position, MD6 Plus Travel Opposite Axis Position, MD7 Neg Travel Opposite Axis Position, MD8 Tote Dump Position, MD9 Soft Travel Lim Pos, MD10 OT Pos, MD11 Base Speed for AutoCycle (steps/min), MD12 Base Acc/Dec for AutoCycle (steps/min^2)/10, MD13...

VISU_MDS COPY FROM OPPOSITE Function: This function is used to duplicate parameters between tippers, likely to ensure consistency or speed up configuration after a motor replacement. The source text does not specify which parameters are copied or any restrictions.

VISU_MDS Unique Axis Parameters: While most Machine Data values should match from machine to machine, MD5 and MD21 are exceptions. These values are determined through physical measurement during alignment and are not transferable between machines or axes.

VISU_IO_DIAG Screen Overview: This screen is part of the Operator Station HMI. It is explicitly noted as read-only and intended for troubleshooting purposes. It includes an informational banner for alarms/messages, temperature readings for the CPU and motherboard, voltage readings for the internal controller, and statuses for station switches and...

VISU_IO_DIAG Control Temps Section: This section provides real-time temperature data for the HMI's central processing unit and motherboard. It is part of the read-only VISU_IO_DIAG troubleshooting screen.

VISU_IO_DIAG Voltage Levels Section: This section provides voltage readings for the internal controller of the HMI. The expected value is 24 V. It is part of the read-only VISU_IO_DIAG troubleshooting screen.

VISU_IO_DIAG Input Details Pop-up: The screen includes sections showing inputs. These sections are interactive; selecting one will open a new window with detailed information about those specific inputs. This is part of the read-only troubleshooting interface.

VISU_ALARM Screen: The Visu_Alarm screen is part of the Operator Station HMI. It provides a list of all tipper alarms, each accompanied by a timestamp. The screen includes a SHOW HISTORY button that, when activated, displays the last 1500 alarm records.
VISU_ALARM History Capacity: The SHOW HISTORY button on the Visu_Alarm screen is configured to retrieve and display the most recent 1500 alarm records for the tipper system.

Tipper Alarms on Operator Station HMI: The Operator Station HMI includes a dedicated screen, Visu_Alarm, for monitoring tipper alarms. Each alarm event is listed with its associated timestamp, allowing operators to track the sequence and timing of tipper faults.

Operator Station HMI CYCLE STOP Button: The operator station main screen includes a CYCLE STOP button. This button is the primary control for stopping the operator station, as per the documented procedure. An image of this screen is available in the manual.

Tipper Jogging Mode: Jogging mode allows manual positioning of the left and right tipper end effectors. It is accessed from the 'Visu_Dual_MCP' screen (F3) on the operator station HMI. The automatic tipping cycle must be stopped by pressing CYCLE STOP before jogging is enabled. Pressing JOG opens the jogging screen.

Tipper Jogging HMI Screen: The jogging screen is accessed by pressing the JOG button on the 'Visu_Dual_MCP' screen (F3) after a CYCLE STOP. It provides manual mode controls for four axes: Z1 (left tipper vertical), A1 (left tipper rotation), Z2 (right tipper vertical), and A2 (right tipper rotation). Each axis has + and – buttons for movement.

HMI CYCLE STOP Control: The CYCLE STOP control is a button on the operator station HMI, specifically mentioned in the context of the 'MCP_Dual' screen. Its function is to stop the tipping cycle, which is a required step when recovering from a non-recoverable motor fault on a tipper.

MCP_Dual Screen (F3): The MCP_Dual screen is accessed by navigating to F3 on the operator station HMI. It is used during non-recoverable fault recovery processes. The screen displays axis statuses for Z1, Z2, A1, and A2, and includes buttons for CYCLE STOP, JOG, RESET, AUTO, and CYCLE START.

Non-Recoverable Fault: AGV Stuck: This fault is verified on the operator station HMI. The OUT Fault Status for the affected tipper should have a value of 82. Recovery involves forcing a value on OUT W1: a value of 3 if the tote and AGV are ready to continue, or 32771 if the AGV needs to go to the hospital.

HMI Screen: Visu_ManControl: The 'Visu_ManControl' screen contains a 'CellIO Status' button. This screen is part of the operator station HMI and is used during the recovery procedure for a non-recoverable AGV stuck fault.

Tipper Z-Axis Linear Bearings Inspection and Lubrication: Visually inspect both Z-axis linear rails for wetness of grease and/or signs of dried grease. If the rails are dry (not wet with grease), lubricate the bearing blocks using automotive bearing grease (e.g., Mobil1). There are two bearing blocks with one standard 1/4-in.

Z-Axis Linear Bearing Lubrication: Visually inspect both Z-axis linear rails for wetness of grease or signs of dried grease. If rails are dry, lubricate the bearing blocks using automotive bearing grease (e.g., Mobil1). There are two bearing blocks with one standard 1/4-in. nipple on each end, totaling four nipples to grease.

Manual Axes Referencing Initiation: To manually reference axes, navigate to the 'Visu_Dual_MCP' screen (F3) on the operator station HMI and press CYCLE STOP to stop the automatic tipping cycle. This allows manual positioning of the end effector.

Set Tipper Controller Parameters: Setting controller parameters is step 2 of tipper commissioning. The operator must navigate to the 'Visu_MDs' screen (F2) on the operator station HMI. Access to change settings requires logging in as maintenance or admin.

HMI Screen: Visu_MDs (F2): The 'Visu_MDs' screen is an HMI screen on the operator station. It is accessed by pressing F2. Its documented use is for setting initial parameters for each axis of the tippers. Changing settings on this screen requires maintenance or admin level login.

OptiSweep software as the integration layer: The speaker states that OptiSweep software integrates everything so that all connected elements talk and work as a team. The slide shows OptiSweep Software among the core elements and visually associates it with other components including UPS Chat, Geek+ AGVs, hospital controller, sorter, printer, and Aveva HMI.

Map overview uses lanes and stations as visual location types: The source describes two variants of location shown on the map. Lanes are described as light blue or grayish square blocks. Stations are described as orange elements. The presenter notes that these are the terms used in this context and that different station settings are discussed on the next slide.

Tipping Station Screen Overview: This HMI screen is part of the OptiSweep system. It is designed to give operators a view of the performance of the tipping station, specifically tracking the number of bags completed, any errors that have occurred, and the time taken for tasks.

Tipping Station Screen Navigation Path: To reach the Tipping Station screen, an operator must first press the SMALLS button, then select 'ACB' from the drop-down menu. Tipping Station Screen Metrics: The screen provides real-time or near-real-time operational data points for the tipping station. The specific metrics mentioned are: a count of completed bags, a count or indication of errors, and a measurement of how long tasks take to complete.

System Shutdown Control: The System Shutdown control is located on the System API Controls screen (Figure 4-9). Its function is to shut down the system. The documented operational constraint is that it should only be done when a sort does not begin when the current sort ends. Upon shutdown, AGVs go to a shutdown queue.

System Close Out Control: The System Close Out control is located on the System API Controls screen (Figure 4-9). Its function is to send all totes to the tippers to close out the sorter. The documented operational constraint is that it should only be done at the end of a sort.

Get Metrics Pop-Up Screen: The Get Metrics pop-up screen (Figure 4-10) is accessed from the System API Controls screen. It provides a view of key operational metrics. The documented metrics include Number of Exchanges, Number of Mis-sorts, and Status.

AGV Remove and Recover Procedure: The Remove AGV control on the AGV API Controls screen is used to take an AGV out of the system. The procedure requires entering the AGV ID. If the AGV has an issue, it must be physically removed. If the AGV is carrying a tote, the tote must be taken to the hospital, where it is removed.

AGV System Recovery Commands: The 'Execute AGV Command' control is used for system recovery in the event that the system goes down and messages are missed. The 'Resend Geek Command' control is also used for system recovery; if Geek+ has a command error, the command guide can be provided and the message will be resent to Geek+.
AGV Status Screen Navigation: The navigation path to the AGV Status screen is a single button press on the AGV STATUS button located in the upper-left corner of the display.
AGV Error Code Display: Active error codes for each AGV are shown on the AGV Status screen. This provides operators with immediate visibility into AGV faults.

Tipper Stats Metrics: The Tipper Stats section provides the following metrics for both the left and right tippers: Totes Processed (total and sent to Hospital Station), Faults (count since last reset), Avg Cycle Time (from gripper taking hold of a tote until release), Avg Totes/Hour (average taken at 15-minute intervals), and Time Starved...

Heartbeat Stats Metrics: The Heartbeat section provides statistics for heartbeat signals between the tipper and the WCS. Metrics include: Last (most recent signal time in ms), Max (longest signal time in ms), and Min (shortest signal time in ms).

Right Tipper Alarm Group: The Right Tipper component has an alarm group named 'AlarmGroup_Helix_RightTipper'. System Startup via HMI: The system startup procedure is initiated from the system HMI. The operator must first navigate to the 'system API screen' and then press the 'SYSTEM STARTUP' button. This is a manual step to begin system operation.

Tipper Axis Homing (Z1/A1, Z2/A2): The left tipper has axes Z1 and A1; the right tipper has axes Z2 and A2. Pressing AUTO REF initiates homing for each axis. During homing, the axis button changes from green to yellow to indicate movement. The tipper motor moves until it senses the home proximity switch, then stops.

Tipper Cycle Start to Ready Position: Once all axes are homed, the operator presses CYCLE START. This command moves the tipper motor from the home position (where it stopped after homing) to a ready position, preparing the tipper for automatic operation.

Tipper AUTO Mode: After the tipper reaches the ready position, the operator places it in AUTO mode. In AUTO mode, the tipper waits for the Warehouse Control System (WCS) to send instructions for automated operation.

System Shutdown Procedure: The system should be shut down between sorts to allow AGVs to charge. The procedure is: 1) On the system HMI, navigate to the system API screen. 2) Press SYSTEM SHUTDOWN. 3) The AGVs go to a shutdown queue.

Tipper Axis Hard Stop Fault: When manually jogging the tipper axes (Z1, Z2, A1, A2), if an operator pushes an axis until it hits a physical hard stop, the axis will register a fault. This is a known condition during manual operation.

HMI Screen: CellIO Status: This screen allows an operator to select a specific tipper and view its OUT Fault Status. It also provides an OUT W1 forced value box and a checkbox to apply the forced value. This interface is used to recover from an AGV stuck fault.

OUT W1 Forced Values for AGV Stuck Recovery: After verifying the AGV stuck fault (OUT Fault Status 82), the operator forces a value on OUT W1. Enter 3 if the tote and AGV are ready to continue working. Enter 32771 if the AGV needs to go to the hospital. The forced value is applied by checking the adjacent box, waiting 10 seconds, and then unchecking it.

If the system is started without this configuration, an AGV without a tote must be manually moved into the zone that is missing an AGV, and the AGV must be added to the RMS...
System Start-Up Timing Requirement: Operators are instructed to start the system 15 minutes prior to the scheduled sort start time.

System Start-Up Sequence: The documented start-up sequence includes: 1. Reset the metrics (to facilitate report generation). 2. Start the system. 3. Close out (Bag Out). After close out is completed, the system goes back to 'Running'. 4. Shut down.

AGV System Start-Up Precondition: The system requires nine (9) AGVs without totes before start-up. These must be positioned with five (5) under the north rack and four (4) under the south rack. If the system is started without this configuration, an AGV without a tote must be manually moved into the deficient zone and added to the RMS.

AGV System Start-Up Sequence: The documented steps are: 1. Reset the metrics (to make pulling reports easier). 2. Start the system. 3. Close out (Bag Out). After close out is completed, the system returns to a 'Running' state.
